About the accent, what Athenaeus 9 p. 408 reports is remarkable: παρὰ τοῖς τραγικοῖς καὶ τοῖς κωμικοῖς παροξυτόνως ἀνέγνωσται χερνίβα [among the tragedians and comedians it is read with an acute accent on the penult, χερνίβα], παρ' Εὐριπίδῃ ἐν Ἡρακλεῖ (929) “εἰς χερνίβ᾽ ὡς βάψειεν Αλκμήνης γόνος” [in Euripides in the Heracles (929) “that the son of Alcmena might dip into the lustral water”], ἀλλὰ καὶ παρ' Ευπόλιδι ἐν Αἰξὶν αὐτοῦ τὴν χερνίβα παύσεις [but also in Eupolis in the Goats “you will stop his lustral water”]. Athenaeus teaches at length that this accent is false, comparing other nouns ending in ψ. From Athenaeus are excerpted the things which are read in the scholium of the Venice codex on Aristophanes Peace 956. The false accent is followed by the scholium on Euripides Alcestis 99: χερνίβ': παροξυτόνως τὴν πηγαίαν χέρνιβα [lustral water: with an acute accent on the penult, the spring lustral water].
What lustral water of the clansmen will receive me?
pouring these lustral waters for the dead.
since Zeus without anger made you a partner of the lustral waters in the house.

Thus Pauwius for χαιρομυσή [polluting the hands]. Aeschylus seems to be imitated by Constantine Manasses Chron. 5151 χαιρομυσῆ λήσταρχον κακεργάτην [a hand-polluting robber-chief, a malefactor], where it is not clear whether he too wrote χερομυσῆ [polluting the hands] or, deceived by a corrupt reading, put χαιρομυσῆ [polluting the hands], and likewise 6083. ἄνδρες τινὲς χαιρομυσεῖς φονίως ἐμπεσόντες [certain hand-polluting men falling murderously], where the manuscripts have χερομισεῖς and χαιρομισεῖς.
